open_points.subject: EXECUTION_STATUS_CONCLUSIONS and NODE_CONCLUSION_EFFECTS
open_points.text: the conclusion each NodeExecution status gives (A13 rules 5 and 7), what each node conclusion means for the run and for its dependants (A13 rules 5 and 7)
open_points.question: What is the closed node-conclusion taxonomy, and what are the exact keys, cell fields and mappings of these two tables? No NodeConclusion model or enumeration is defined, so implementations cannot determine where status-to-conclusion mapping ends and conclusion-to-run/dependant behavior begins.
options: Add a NodeConclusion enumeration and enumerate both tables completely
Use NodeExecutionStatus directly as the node-conclusion taxonomy and enumerate the run/dependant effects for every status
Replace the two tables with one fully enumerated table keyed by NodeExecutionStatus
open_points.default_guess: Add an explicit NodeConclusion enumeration and publish total literal mappings for both tables.

open_points.subject: outcome_unknown conclusion correspondence
open_points.text: a table here keyed by the enumeration, total over its members, whose cells name members
open_points.question: How can EXECUTION_STATUS_CONCLUSIONS give one table value for `outcome_unknown` when A11 rule 3 makes its conclusion depend on the associated EffectAttempt state and, when resolved `applied`, on whether the binding has output ports?
options: Map `outcome_unknown` to a distinct contextual conclusion that `effects.operation_element_conclusion` resolves from the attempt and binding
Permit table cells to name a resolver or conditional rule rather than only an enumeration member
Exclude `outcome_unknown` from this correspondence and keep its complete interpretation in `effects`
open_points.default_guess: Map `outcome_unknown` to an explicit contextual conclusion and leave its resolution to `effects.operation_element_conclusion`.
